title: introduce-cost-rule-exporter-cli-and-quant-sentinel-monitor
author: Lina Park
release_notes: Added a new CLI to export tenant-level cost-rule suggestions from runtime telemetry and a runtime monitor that flags quantization-induced unit-econ regressions. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation:
We frequently get requests to translate raw runtime telemetry into actionable, tenant-scoped defaults (batching/caching/quant profiles) for Dedicated and Private customers. SRE and Cost Ops workflows require a deterministic artifact that ties observed token-level telemetry to suggested policy changes (rules as code). Separately, recent rollouts of quantized variants have produced subtle unit-quality regressions that are only visible when comparing in-flight responses to eval baselines. This PR delivers two pieces: (1) a small CLI 'cost-rule-exporter' that consumes aggregated telemetry snapshots (token latencies, batch shapes, cache hit rates, model variants) and produces a versioned YAML of suggested cost-rules, and (2) a lightweight 'quant-sentinel' monitor integrated into the rollout pipeline that computes a per-tenant quality delta and surfaces rule-suggested rollbacks when thresholds are crossed.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds cmd/cost-rule-exporter: a Go CLI that ingests telemetry parquet/ndjson, runs a set of heuristics and scoring rules, and writes a ruleset.yaml suitable for tenant import. The heuristics encapsulate batching/caching/quantization tradeoffs and include conservative fallbacks.
- Adds pkg/telemetry/mapper: transforms runtime metrics into economic signals (tokens-per-second, cold-prefill-rate, effective-batch-size distribution, kv-cache-hit-rate).
- Adds pkg/quant/sentinel: a small worker that compares golden evals with sampled production responses (optionally via trace tags) and emits a labeled incident if quality delta > configurable threshold.
- Integrates the sentinel as an optional check in the rollout pipeline (release/rollout.go) so canary jobs fail fast and suggest auto-revert with the exported rules.
- Documentation and an end-to-end example: docs/cost-rule-exporter.md and examples/cost-rule-dryrun.yaml.

Checklist (manual):
- [x] Design doc: ENG-4120 linked
- [x] CLI basic tests and integration smoke test
- [x] Add unit coverage for telemetry mapper heuristics
- [x] Add sentinel regression detector and e2e smoke in CI
- [x] Docs and example import/export

Design notes / heuristics: 
- The exporter runs a two-stage pipeline: (A) profile extraction (shape histograms + KV cache summaries) and (B) rule synthesis. Each candidate rule is scored by a simulated unit-econ delta (cost tokens saved vs expected quality impact) using conservative priors. Rules above a configured score threshold are emitted.
- Quant-sentinel uses paired-sample evaluation: sample N responses from the quantized variant and compare to the baseline using the same eval rubric used by the quality team (BLEU/embedding-sim + task-specific heuristics). We smooth with an adaptive window to avoid false positives on micro-drifts.
- Safety: exporter includes a 'safe_mode' that only proposes non-breaking defaults (batching up to X, cache TTL shorter than Y) and a 'dry-run' mode that emits a simulated impact report.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests for telemetry normalization and rule scoring (pkg/telemetry/*)
- Integration test: take a recorded workload snapshot (tests/fixtures/tenant-heatmap.ndjson) and assert the exported ruleset contains expected keys and monotonic scoring of batching suggestions.
- Sentinel smoke: run paired sample with the small synthetic harness in testdata/quant-sentinel and assert no false-positive for known-good deltas.

Rollout plan:
- Canary the CLI in infra-tooling for a small set of internal tenants (cost-ops team).
- Enable quant-sentinel for the next handful of quantized model rollouts behind a feature flag (rollout.safe_quant_monitor=true).
- After 2 weeks of stable telemetry and no false positives, flip default to enabled for enterprise tenants on Dedicated.

Backward compatibility / breaking changes:
- None. New CLI and monitor are opt-in. Exported YAML follows 'rules-as-code' schema v0.2 and importers will ignore unknown keys.

Related work:
- References: ENG-4120 (design), ENG-4172 (quality rubric integration), SUP-1298 (customer request for tenant defaults export)

Commits summary:
- 7 commits: initial CLI skeleton -> telemetry mapper -> scoring engine -> sentinel worker -> doc + examples -> tests -> CI fixes

Files changed (high level):
- cmd/cost-rule-exporter/main.go (CLI entrypoint)
- cmd/cost-rule-exporter/README.md (usage + examples)
- pkg/telemetry/mapper.go (shape histograms, KV summaries)
- pkg/telemetry/score_engine.go (rule scoring and simulation)
- pkg/quant/sentinel.go (paired-sample regression detector)
- release/rollout.go (optional sentinel gate integration)
- docs/cost-rule-exporter.md (how-to + safety notes)
- examples/cost-rule-dryrun.yaml (sample output)
- tests/* (unit and integration harnesses)

Breaking out the large changes into smaller commits helped reviewers focus on the scoring model and sentinel logic separately.

Operational impact and observability:
- The exported rulesets are versioned and stored in internal bucket s3://redwood-cost-rules/{tenant}/{timestamp}. The exporter emits telemetry metrics: exporter.run.duration, exporter.rules.count, exporter.simulated_saving_usd.
- Quant-sentinel exposes metrics: sentinel.window_size, sentinel.false_positive_rate (estimated), sentinel.alerts.count. Alerts integrate to PagerDuty and cost-ops Slack channel.

Security notes:
- CLI reads telemetry from an internal read-only telemetry export S3 location; credentials are scoped. Exported YAML never contains PII; only aggregated histograms and tenant id. Sentinels operate on sampled responses with trace tags stripped.

Next steps after merge:
- Wire the exporter into the Cost Ops UI for a one-click preview/import flow (follow-up ENG ticket).
- Add an autorun mode that periodically proposes candidate rule PRs for tenant defaults (opt-in).
commits: feat(telemetry): implement mapper for shape histograms and kv summaries
feat(scoring): add simulation-based rule scorer and conservative priors
chore(docs): add exporter README and usage examples
test: add unit and integration tests for mapper and scorer
ci: fix lint and add sentinel smoke test to pipeline
review_thread:
Tomás Nguyen (reviewer): Left high-level comments on the scoring priors; suggested making the default threshold more conservative to avoid churn.
Author response: lowered default score threshold from 0.25 -> 0.4 and added safe_mode which emits only non-breaking rules.

Priya Kapoor (reviewer): Asked for clearer docs on how exported rules map to tenant defaults in the UI.
Author response: added docs/cost-rule-exporter.md and example import YAML. Added a note about schema v0.2 compatibility.

Ethan Li (reviewer): Requested sentinel to expose a per-tenant TTL and to limit sampling rate to reduce egress costs.
Author response: added sampling_rate config and per-tenant ttl to sentinel; updated tests and CI smoke.

CI: initial run failed due to linter. Author: fixed gofmt and adjusted import ordering. CI: subsequent run passed.
Maintainer (merge): Approved and squashed commits.
